newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Mobile phone use seen surging in Portugal by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phone use seen surging in Portugal by 2000.

text.p: The mobile phone market is booming in Portugal with up to one in five Portuguese likely to own a phone by the end of the century, analysts said on Wednesday.
About one in 20 Portuguese currently own a mobile phone, supplied by either Telecel-Comunicacoes Pessoais or Telecomunicacoes Moveis Nacionais (TMN), a unit of Portugal Telecom.
A 35.6 percent stake in Telecel will be floated in Lisbon by December 10 and analysts said they expected strong demand due to the sector's growth potential.
The penetration rate for mobile phones in Italy is around eight percent, in Spain about four percent, in Britain more than 10 percent and in Nordic countries above 20 percent.
"I would not be surprised if in 2000 market penetration were about 20 percent, or two million people," said Joao Morais, director of research at Portuguese bank Banco Finantia.
Diego Hernando, analyst at Lisbon broker Midas, said: "There could be penetration of 15 or 16 percent by the year 2000. That is an average annual growth of customers of about 30 percent."

Kurt Hellstrom of Eriksson Radio said the number of mobile phone users in Portugal could reach one million by the end of 1997 and 1.5 million in 1998, up from around 415,000 in June and analysts' forecasts of 600,000 at the end of 1996.
The number of users grew by 79.4 percent in the 12 months to June, according to figures from Telecel and TMN.
Most analysts said the strong demand would make the entry of a third operator by 1998 inevitable, although the new company would probably not have much impact on Telecel and TMN initially.
"The market is booming, and a third operator should start to operate in 1998," said one analyst, estimating it could take around 10 percent of the local market between 1998 and 2000.
Analysts said revenues from mobile phone use in Portugal could more than double by 2000 despite a drop in phone charges.

"In the year 2000, allowing for falls in tariffs, revenues from the sales of mobile phones and additional services could reach 250 billion escudos ($1.62 billion) or more, up from 100 billion now," said Finantia's Morais.

Analysts said costs of mobile phone equipment had plunged since Telecel entered the market in 1992 and said they expected tariffs to fall further as fixed costs declined due to increased market penetration.
Telecel earns 17,200 escudos a month on average per client and TMN earns about 13,000.
Morais forecast the average tariff per minute would drop by between 40 and 50 percent to 30 to 40 escudos by 2000.
"This decline will be continuous and gradual," he said.
Despite that the growth of the mobile phone sector will boost the results of the two main operators, analysts said.
In the first half of 1996 Telecel's net profit was 2.6 billion escudos, up from 151 million a year earlier.
TMN posted a profit of more than two billion escudos in the first half of 1996, compared with a loss of 1.5 billion escudos in the same year-ago period.

"Telecel is expected to post a net profit of seven billion escudos in 1996 and 10 billion in 1997, while TMN could make between four and five billion in 1996 and eight to 10 billion in 1997," said Midas's Hernando. "1998 will depend on the level of competition (from a third operator)." ($1=154.0 Escudo)
